mainEntity.name: How long does sensitivity last after getting a dental crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild sensitivity following crown placement typically resolves within 2-4 weeks as the tooth adapts to its restoration. This sensitivity usually decreases gradually over time. If sensitivity persists beyond a month or becomes more severe, contact your dentist for evaluation, as this may indicate the need for additional treatment or adjustment.

mainEntity.name: Can a tooth die after crown treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whilst most teeth remain vital after crown treatment, occasional loss of vitality can occur, particularly in teeth that were already compromised before treatment. Modern conservative preparation techniques significantly reduce this risk. Your dentist monitors crowned teeth during regular check-ups and can detect any changes in vitality through clinical examination.

mainEntity.name: Will I need root canal treatment before getting a crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Root canal treatment is not routinely required before crown placement. However, if your tooth has extensive decay, large existing fillings, or shows signs of pulp damage, your dentist may recommend root canal treatment first. This decision depends on individual clinical assessment and aims to support long-term treatment success.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my crowned tooth is healthy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Healthy crowned teeth should feel comfortable during normal function, with no persistent pain or temperature sensitivity. The gum tissue around the crown should appear pink and healthy, without swelling or bleeding. Regular dental check-ups include assessment of crowned teeth to monitor ongoing health and proper function.

mainEntity.name: Are there alternatives to crowns that preserve more tooth structure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Depending on the extent of tooth damage, alternatives such as large fillings, inlays, or onlays may preserve more natural tooth structure. However, when significant tooth structure is missing or weakened, crowns often provide the most reliable long-term protection. You may also find our guide on composite bonding versus crowns helpful when weighing your options. Your dentist will recommend the most appropriate treatment based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my crown feels uncomfortable weeks after placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contact your dentist if discomfort persists beyond the expected healing period or if symptoms worsen over time. Your dentist can assess the crown's fit, check your bite alignment, and evaluate the underlying tooth's health. Most comfort issues can be resolved through minor adjustments or additional treatment if needed.
